findings.evidence: A confirmed pending request retained an obsolete draft version; retry and token renewal could not resolve it and a new request was blocked by the client pending intent.
The split editor required original attachments to be selected again, but an empty file-list autosave could clear the missing marker; the backend did not store that state or enforce it on publication.
A publisher reassigned to another college could replay an old request ID and receive the previous college full publication view; the real new regression returned 200 before the scope check fix.

source_notes: After the 70-test run, only the module docstring and backup comment were clarified to state the snapshot/RPO limit; executable behavior and tests did not change. Syntax and diff checks passed afterward.

history_notes: The first post-change run had 18 passes and 1 failure because an unchanged-receipt assertion compared entire live projections containing evaluation times. The final assertion compares exact rows from six business tables plus recipient IDs, retaining stronger content/delivery invariants. The original log is preserved.
The 20-case intermediate green preceded the minimal owner-receipt permission refinement and the new cross-college case. It is historical evidence; the 70-case run is the final targeted result.
70 includes all 21 new cases and 49 existing cases. Repeated runs are not added as unique test counts.

api_contract.ownership: Current publisher role remains necessary. Request records are scoped by owner. A previously committed own request returns only its minimal operation receipt after a scope/college change; full publication POST replay and detail access retain current college/scope checks.
api_contract.rate_limit: 60 cancellation attempts per current owner per hour using the existing application limiter
api_contract.attachment_names: At most 3 nonblank names, each 1..255 characters. They are metadata only. Omission preserves prior pending names; an explicit empty array resolves the missing-attachment gate.

verified_behavior: Cancel and publish compete within BEGIN IMMEDIATE; exactly one durable outcome is observed.
A publication already parsed before cancellation is denied after the cancellation commits.
Repeated cancellation and a lost first response do not create a second decision or publish anything.
Cancelling an already committed request leaves exact publication, original, delivery, notice and source rows unchanged.
The same request ID in another account has independent state; a student or anonymous user cannot cancel as a publisher.
Missing attachment names survive reload and a legacy text-only save; publication remains blocked until explicit resolution.
Restored cancelled IDs remain blocked after fresh organizational grants; restore itself does not regrant campus authority.
The personal export includes only this owner cancellation records; a portable import into another account does not restore those request states.
Deleting the account cascades cancellation records while retaining other owners records.
A pre-extension database adds an empty ledger; a present marker with missing table or unsupported future version refuses startup and restore.

boundaries: Original publication payload is durable in owner-scoped edit-cache before external publishing; retries retain request_id and original draft version.
New input uses a separate server draft; unresolved attachment names are explicit metadata, never claimed as copied files.
Stopping an uncertain publication uses a server tombstone, not local cache deletion; published receipts do not withdraw or restore notices.
Warm ordinary lists merge only lightweight clock fields; unchanged display values cause no page read or DOM paint.
Sensitive filters refill the full loaded range only on relevant signature changes; unknown or changed stable projection revisions also force a real range refresh.
A stale time-sensitive cursor reloads the previous range plus the requested next page without showing a first-page-only intermediate state.
Board requests explicitly use sort=board; list requests retain their original sort.
